classification.difficultyReason: Follow the supplied progression from derivative to gradients and line equations, then find axis intercepts and apply the right-triangle area formula.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that $y=\sin^2 x$ has derivative $y'=2\sin x\cos x$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the gradients of the tangent and normal to $y=\sin^2 x$ at the point where $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$.

answer.worked:
At $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$:
$$\begin{align*}y'&=2\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\\&=2\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)\\&=1.\end{align*}$$
Gradient of tangent $=1$.

Gradient of normal $=-\frac{1}{1}=-1$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the equations of the tangent and normal to $y=\sin^2 x$ at the point where $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Suppose that the tangent meets the $x$-axis at $P$, the normal meets the $y$-axis at $Q$ and $O$ is the origin. Show that $\triangle OPQ$ has area $\frac{\pi^2-4}{32}$ units$^2$.

spec.description: Unscaled coordinate sketch of the blue curve, red tangent and green normal, with arrowheads at both ends. Axes have no ticks, grid or origin label. Ordinary axes are black under house style.
spec.mathematics: Curve y=sin²x; tangent y=x−π/4+1/2 and normal y=−x+π/4+1/2 meet at (π/4,1/2).
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied question diagram, visible in student and answer editions.

answer.worked:
The tangent $x-y=\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac12$ meets the $x$-axis where $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac12,\\P&=\left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac12,0\right).\end{align*}$$
The normal $x+y=\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac12$ meets the $y$-axis where $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac12,\\Q&=\left(0,\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac12\right).\end{align*}$$
Since the coordinate axes are perpendicular,
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{Area}(\triangle OPQ)&=\frac12|OP||OQ|\\&=\frac12\left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac12\right)\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac12\right)\\&=\frac12\left[\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)^2-\left(\frac12\right)^2\right]\\&=\frac12\left(\frac{\pi^2}{16}-\frac14\right)\\&=\frac1{32}(\pi^2-4)\\&=\frac{\pi^2-4}{32}\text{ units}^2.\end{align*}$$
